title: Harris v. Avery (1869)
summary: Claims for slander and false imprisonment arising from the same encounter could be joined.
notes:
Federal Rule 18 later permits broad joinder of claims against an existing opposing party without this same-transaction limitation. Jurisdiction must still be established separately.

Harris demurred for misjoinder; the district court overruled the demurrer and the Kansas Supreme Court affirmed, reading the code to permit joinder of claims arising out of 'the same transaction or transactions connected with the same subject of action' and finding that the accusation, taking of the horse, arrest and four-or-five-day confinement with felons formed one transaction.

sections.Parties: Avery sued Harris concerning an accusation of theft, seizure of a horse, and detention.
sections.Material Facts: The alleged episode involved an accusation that Avery had stolen a horse and events leading to his confinement for several days. Avery sought relief for more than one legal wrong within that episode. Harris objected to combining the theories in a single action.
sections.Procedural History: The Kansas court upheld joinder under the applicable procedural statute.
sections.Issue: Could the plaintiff join the slander and false-imprisonment claims arising from the episode?
sections.Holding: Yes. Their different legal labels did not prevent treating them as arising from the same transaction.
sections.Reasoning: The court read the transaction requirement in terms of the connected events giving rise to the controversy. Trying the associated claims together could avoid fragmenting a single dispute. The decision is part of the chapter’s account of movement away from rigid separation by forms of action.

learning.why: Claims for slander and false imprisonment arising from the same encounter could be joined.

topics.cp-claim-joinder: Different legal wrongs could be joined when they arose from the same transaction.
topics.cp-transaction: The episode supplied the connection between the slander and imprisonment claims.
topics.cp-frcp-18: The Kansas code's transaction-based joinder is the historical antecedent of Rule 18's unlimited claim joinder.

mnemonic.rationale: Called a horse thief and jailed
